That said `maxFeePerGas` and `maxPriorityFeePerGas` aren't the most end-user friendly terms. Would we consider updating EIP-1559 to use `tip` and `maxFee` terminology? fyi i think the latest preferred term for `tip` is priority fee 🙂 I guess the next question is whether the JSONRPC result should contain the "max" or "actual" ~tip~ priority fee. i suggested changing the terms a couple weeks ago, but <@!301186049323958275> made the point that the spec should be as pedantic as possible and we can choose the lay terms external to the spec yep, good questions i don't have a preference, but IMO if the actual tip is included then we should also include the effectiveGasPrice since both depend on retrieving the block's base fee from disk ya in my first-pass implementation of the JSONRPC fields I re-used `gasPrice` as the effective gas price for -1559 txs: https://github.com/quilt/go-ethereum/pull/48/commits/7b11019893be78d3797c9ebdd58d7fcfd8ea85bf#diff-c426ecd2f7d247753b9ea8c1cc003f21fa412661c1f967d203d4edf8163da344R1277. excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: AFAIK there haven't been any EIPs drafted for the tx changes, only the `baseFee` additions to the block results (EIP-3041 and friends).  _Personally_ I like the `maxFee` and `tip` names used in your geth PR, but IMO I think the field names in the JSONRPC and the EIP itself should match as closely as possible.  That said `maxFeePerGas` and `maxPriorityFeePerGas` aren't the most end-user friendly terms.  Would we consider updating EIP-1559 to use `tip` and `maxFee` terminology?
